parts.zh: W: 嗨，戴维。我快两周没在课堂上见到你了
M: 嗨，莎拉。唉，说来话长
W: 哦，是的。今年冬天有好多病毒在传播
M: 还有，在从医院回来的路上
W: 哦，那太糟糕了！真是太倒霉了！
M: 更糟糕的是，我偏偏摔在了四个九年级女生面前
W: 天啊，这真是彻头彻尾的灾难！笔记本电脑还在保修期内吗？如果是的话
M: 保修期在我摔坏它的前三天就过了
W: 听我说，我家里有一家又好又实惠的电脑维修店的电话
M: 哇，谢谢你，莎拉！那太好了！我先给我妈妈打个电话
M: 但既然你的资历非常适合写历史小说

items.stem: What does Sarah think David was doing for the last two weeks?

choices.text: He was enjoying his holiday.
He was recovering in hospital.
He was busy writing his essays.
He was fighting a throat infection.
choices.zh: 他在与喉咙感染作斗争。

items.stem: What happened to David on his way back from the hospital?

choices.text: He broke his wrist.
He lost his antibiotics.
He slipped on ice and fell.
He was laughed at by some girls.

items.stem: What does Sarah say they should do with the damaged computer?

choices.text: Turn to her father for help.
Call the repair shop to fix it.
choices.zh: 打电话给维修店修理它。

choices.text: Ask the manufacturer for repairs.
Replace it with a brand-new one.

items.stem: What does Sarah say she is going to do?

choices.text: Help David retrieve his essays.
choices.zh: 帮助 David 找回他的论文。

choices.text: Introduce David to her parents.
choices.zh: 把 David 介绍给她的父母。

choices.text: Offer David some refreshments.
choices.zh: 给 David 提供一些茶点。

choices.text: Accompany David to his home.

items.stem: What does the man say about the woman?

choices.text: She is a critic of works on military affairs.
choices.zh: 她是军事著作的评论家。

choices.text: She is an acclaimed hostess of Book Talk.
choices.zh: 她是《书话》节目广受赞誉的主持人。

choices.text: She is a researcher of literary genres.
choices.zh: 她是文学体裁的研究者。

choices.text: She is a historian of military history.

items.stem: What does the woman say about her newly published book?

choices.text: It is about the military history of Europe.
choices.zh: 它是关于欧洲军事史的。

choices.text: It is set in the 18th and 19th centuries.
choices.zh: 它以18世纪和19世纪为背景。

choices.text: It is her fifth book of military history.
choices.zh: 它是她的第五本军事史著作。

choices.text: It is a war novel set in the future.
choices.zh: 它是一部以未来为背景的战争小说。

items.stem: What did the woman do before writing her new book?

choices.text: She visited soldiers' wives and mothers.
choices.zh: 她拜访了士兵的妻子和母亲。

choices.text: She conducted surveys of many soldiers.
choices.zh: 她对许多士兵进行了调查。

choices.text: She met a large number of soldiers in person.
She looked into the personal lives of soldiers.
choices.zh: 她调查了士兵的个人生活。

items.stem: What does the woman say about her writing history books?

choices.text: She doesn't have much freedom for imagination.
choices.zh: 她没有太多想象的自由。

choices.text: It is not easy to make her readers believe in her.
choices.zh: 让读者相信她并不容易。

choices.text: It is difficult to attract young readers.
She has to combine fact with fiction.
choices.zh: 她必须把事实与虚构结合起来。

items.stem: What does the passage say appears in almost all ads for Coca-Cola?

choices.text: Santa Claus.
A polar bear.
Cocoa seeds.
A glass bottle.

items.stem: Why did the Coca-Cola Company decide to have special packaging designed?

choices.text: To attract customer attention.
To keep up with the times.
To combat counterfeits.
To promote its sales.

items.stem: What do we learn about the Coca-Cola bottle designed by the Root Glass Company?

choices.text: It resembles a picture in the encyclopedia.
choices.zh: 它类似于百科全书中的一幅图片。

choices.text: It appears in the shape of a cocoa seed.
It has the drink's logo in the middle.
choices.zh: 它的中间有该饮料的标识。

choices.text: It displays the image of Santa Claus.
choices.zh: 它展示圣诞老人的形象。

items.stem: What does research show about a conversation between strangers?

choices.text: It often occurs among commuters.
choices.zh: 它经常发生在通勤者之间。

choices.text: It promotes mutual understanding.
It improves their mood considerably.
choices.zh: 它大大改善他们的心情。

choices.text: It takes a great deal of effort to sustain.
choices.zh: 它需要付出很大努力来维持。

items.stem: What prevents people from starting conversation with strangers?

choices.text: Social anxiety.
Excessive caution.
Lack of social skills.
Preference for solitude.

items.stem: Why does a negative encounter with strangers stick in one's memory?

choices.text: People usually regard it as an unforgettable lesson.
choices.zh: 人们通常把它视为难忘的教训。

choices.text: Human brains tend to dwell on negative events.
choices.zh: 人类大脑倾向于纠结于负面事件。

choices.text: Negative events often hurt people deeply.
choices.zh: 负面事件往往深深伤害人们。

choices.text: People generally resent being rejected.

items.stem: What does the passage say the pleasure of connection seems to be?

choices.text: Contagious.
Temporary.
Unpredictable.
Measurable.

items.stem: What does the speaker say about the economy of the Caribbean islands?

choices.text: It depends heavily on tourism.
It is flourishing in foreign trade.
choices.zh: 它在对外贸易方面蓬勃发展。

choices.text: It is mainly based on agriculture.
It relies chiefly on mineral export.

items.stem: What is the main product of the Caribbean islands?

choices.text: Tobacco.
Bananas.
Coffee.
Sugar.

items.stem: What do we learn about the majority of people in the Caribbean islands?

choices.text: They toil on farms.
They live a poor life.
They live in Spanish-style houses.
choices.zh: 他们住在西班牙风格的房子里。

choices.text: They hire people to do housework.

items.stem: What will happen to children if they always get immediate satisfaction?

choices.text: They will be more demanding of their next generation.
choices.zh: 他们会对下一代提出更多要求。

choices.text: They will end up lonely, dependent and dissatisfied.
choices.zh: 他们最终会变得孤独、依赖且不满足。

choices.text: They will experience more setbacks than successes.
choices.zh: 他们经历的挫折会多于成功。

choices.text: They will find it difficult to get along with others.
choices.zh: 他们会发现难以与他人相处。

items.stem: What may prevent parents from raising confident and capable children?

choices.text: Failure to pay due attention to their behavior.
choices.zh: 未能对他们的行为给予应有的关注。

choices.text: Unwillingness to allow them to play with toys.
Unwillingness to satisfy their wishes immediately.
choices.zh: 不愿意立即满足他们的愿望。

choices.text: Failure to spend sufficient quality time with them.
choices.zh: 未能与他们共度足够的高质量时间。

items.stem: Why should children be encouraged to keep trying when they fail?

choices.text: It will enable them to learn from mistakes.
choices.zh: 这将使他们能够从错误中学习。

choices.text: It will help them to handle disappointment.
choices.zh: 这将帮助他们应对失望。

choices.text: It will do much good to their mental health.
choices.zh: 这将对他们的心理健康大有裨益。

choices.text: It will build their ability to endure hardships
choices.zh: 这将培养他们承受艰难困苦的能力。

items.stem: What does the speaker say can easily prevent an interviewee from getting a job?

choices.text: Failing to make sufficient preparations.
Looking away from the hiring manager.
Saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
Making a wrong judgment of the interview.

items.stem: What should the interviewee avoid doing in an interview?

choices.text: Complaining about their previous job.
Inquiring about their salary to be paid.
Exaggerating their academic background.
Understating their previous achievements.

items.stem: What kind of employees do companies like to recruit?

choices.text: Those who have both skill and experience.
choices.zh: 既有技能又有经验的人。

choices.text: Those who get along well with colleagues.
Those who take initiative in their work.
choices.zh: 在工作中主动采取行动的人。

choices.text: Those who are loyal to their managers.

items.stem: What is especially important for those working in a small company?

choices.text: Ability to shoulder new responsibilities.
Experience of performing multiple roles.
Readiness to work to flexible schedules.
choices.zh: 准备好按照灵活的时间表工作。

choices.text: Skills to communicate with colleagues.
